Title: SpeakON: A MagSafe AI device for a post-keyboard world | Product Hunt
# SpeakON. ## A MagSafe AI device for a post-keyboard world. SpeakON was ranked #4 of the week for April 22nd, 2026. SpeakON was ranked #1 of the day for April 22nd, 2026. ### Trending products. I know what hardware costs, not just in money, but in decisions you make at 2am about components that may or may not arrive, about inventory that ties up capital for months before a single unit ships. @rockzhang For someone juggling workshop notes, how does SpeakON handle longer captures; like a 2-min ramble on "Hunter outreach tactics" and pipe them cleanly into Notion or Google Docs without losing the flow? That’s exactly what we designed SpeakON for. And because it works as an input method, you can use it seamlessly across any app — Slack, email, iMessage, anywhere you type. SpeakON really shines on mobile / on the go. But the moment I’m away from the screen — walking, between meetings, in a cab — I switch to SpeakON almost entirely. I’m happy to say it performs great most of the time—it's designed to focus solely on your voice. Actually, it works in any app where you can use a keyboard. It's have a keyboard app also named "SpeakON" to work with the SpeakON hardware. @rockzhang Was the security of the device's data also considered? Works-while-locked is the specific feature that turns it from "nice voice note app" to "don't lose the thought." Curious how SpeakON handles privacy review when it inserts text into apps that have never explicitly granted clipboard or accessibility permissions. This allows for a seamless, 'it just works' experience across any app you're using. Does this mean that I don't have to go through the "switch keyboard, start the voice to text app, switch back to the app..." loop every time I want to speech to text? When you're out for a walk or suddenly hit with a burst of inspiration right before bed, you can use this little device to quickly record your thoughts—all without ever having to unlock your phone. If it lives on the back of your phone, it’s already in your hand 100 times a day.

results.title: SpeakON: A MagSafe AI device for a post-keyboard world | Product Hunt
results.content:
Title: SpeakON: A MagSafe AI device for a post-keyboard world | Product Hunt
A MagSafe AI device for iPhone — press once to speak into any app. Wispr Flow: Dictation That Works Everywhere. Hey Product Hunt — Ryan here, founder of SpeakON. I’ve noticed something about how I work (and probably a lot of you too): Most of the day isn’t thinking — it’s translating thoughts into text. You have something clear in your head — a decision, a reply, a direction — and then you have to stop, open your phone, switch apps, type it out… And somehow that tiny bit of friction is enough to slow everything down. With SpeakON, you press once, speak, and it goes where it needs to go. We intentionally focus on short, high-frequency expression moments — quick replies, decisions, thoughts on the go — instead of long recordings. And because it works as an input method, you can use it seamlessly across any app — Slack, email, iMessage, anywhere you type. But the moment I’m away from the screen — walking, between meetings, in a cab — I switch to SpeakON almost entirely. Actually, it works in any app where you can use a keyboard. It's have a keyboard app also named "SpeakON" to work with the SpeakON hardware. MagSafe-AI-button as a hardware shortcut into any iPhone app is an underrated primitive — shortcuts apps never crossed the friction threshold. Works-while-locked is the specific feature that turns it from "nice voice note app" to "don't lose the thought." Curious how SpeakON handles privacy review when it inserts text into apps that have never explicitly granted clipboard or accessibility permissions. The hardware transmits data directly to the app, which has full system access. This allows for a seamless, 'it just works' experience across any app you're using. Does this mean that I don't have to go through the "switch keyboard, start the voice to text app, switch back to the app..." loop every time I want to speech to text? @tom\_j Exactly — you press and speak, and the text goes directly into whatever app you’re using. SpeakON is about **thinking while speaking, and getting structured output in real time**. Press → speak becomes a very instinctive motion — almost like a reflex.
